messages:
Oliver: Quick follow-up from today's all-hands pricing/packaging section. Two things my team asked that I didn't want to lose track of: 1) exact UTC/time-of-day when dev sandbox credits reset, and 2) how streaming responses affect token billing (do aborted/partial streams still consume credits?). Also curious who is eligible for the rollover pilot Leah mentioned.

Leah (CEO): Short answers: sandbox credits reset at 00:00 UTC on the 1st. Streaming tokens are billed as they are emitted (so partial/aborted streams currently still generate usage). Rollover pilot will be opt-in and limited to a small set of developer-heavy orgs; product will reach out to invitees.

Sana (Finance): To add: default dev sandboxes do NOT roll over today. Enterprise SOWs can request rollover/buffer credits. For billing specifics: we record billing events when the token generation is committed by the runtime; that means a cancelled stream can still produce billed tokens depending on where it was cut off. We know this causes friction and are exploring improved heuristics for final-acceptance billing.

Priya (Product): FWIW, the pilot acceptance criteria will prioritize orgs with heavy dev/test usage patterns and reasonable size (no noisy-neighbor risk). We'll publish a short FAQ and an opt-in flow in Console. Also noting action: draft RFC for "final-acceptance" billing heuristics (to consider not charging for <n> tokens if user cancels within x ms).

Jamal (SRE): Quick technical Q: for CI/test exemptions, are we planning header-based ephemeral tokens or account-level toggles? We need to ensure exemptions don't bypass SLO enforcement or KV-cache accounting. Prefer ephemeral tokens (short TTL) + auditability.

Leah (CEO): Plan is both: org-admin opt-in allowances in Console for planned tests, and ephemeral header tokens for CI. Both will be logged/audited.

Jamal (SRE): Cool. Example header we discussed earlier:

curl -H "Authorization: Bearer <ephemeral-token>" -H "X-Redwood-Test-Exempt: true" 
  -d '{"input":"..."}' https://api.redwood.com/v1/generate

We still need to confirm that metrics pipeline tags these requests and that billing events include the exemption flag. I'll open a ticket for infra validation.

Sana (Finance): Guardrails we're proposing: auto-approve for small ephemeral tokens (<=100k tokens/day), manager-review for 100k-1M, full finance review >1M in a billing period. All exemptions will appear in the billing exports and CSVs we provide to org owners.

Kai (Sales): For customer comms: how will we represent the pilot/rollover in SOWs and self-serve pages? Need a one-liner + FAQ for CS. If pilot is invite-only, can we get a short template to send to prospect customers?

Priya (Product): Yes, we'll prepare a two-sentence description + FAQ card for CS/sales and a short email template for invitees. Also adding a Console flag so org owners can opt in (for invited orgs only during pilot).

OpsBot: Draft internal doc: https://redwood.internal/docs/pricing/credits-rollover-and-exemptions (internal link). (bot)

Oliver: Awesome, thanks everyone. Action items I'll track: 1) Jamal to open infra validation ticket for exemption tagging & billing events, 2) Priya to add pilot criteria + CS template, 3) Sana to publish the guardrail thresholds. I'll file a GH issue and tag the owners. :thumbsup:

Leah (CEO): Thanks Oliver  we'll prioritize the RFCs and pilot outreach.

Priya (Product): Ack, creating the RFC today and will ping the thread when live.

Jamal (SRE): I'll post the infra ticket link here once created.

Sana (Finance): I'll post the proposed thresholds and a short FAQ in #all-hands-followup after product locks the RFC.

Kai (Sales): Will wait for the CS template, thanks.
